pharm: Binds V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle to cause vasoconstriction via the Gq/phospholipase C pathway and intracellular calcium release, and stimulates V2 receptors to promote antidiuresis
quick: Septic shock 0.01-0.07 units/min IV; post-cardiotomy shock 0.03-0.1 units/min IV
No human data; clearance rises in 2nd/3rd trimester so dose may need increasing; may cause uterine contractions
Not addressed in labeling for this use
Mainly metabolized; ~6% excreted unchanged; no specific adjustment stated
Blood pressure, cardiac index, serum sodium, fluid status and urine output
summary: Vasopressin injection is a vasopressor indicated to increase blood pressure in adults with vasodilatory shock who remain hypotensive despite fluids and catecholamines. It is given as a continuous IV infusion titrated to the lowest effective dose, with monitoring of hemodynamics and serum sodium. After discontinuation patients may develop reversible diabetes insipidus.
indications: To increase blood pressure in adults with vasodilatory shock who remain hypotensive despite fluids and catecholamines

dosage.d: Start 0.01 units/min IV; titrate up by 0.005 units/min every 10-15 min to target BP
dosage.n: Limited data above 0.07 units/min; adverse reactions increase at higher doses

dosage.d: Start 0.03 units/min IV; titrate up by 0.005 units/min every 10-15 min to target BP
dosage.n: Limited data above 0.1 units/min for post-cardiotomy shock

dosage.r: After BP stable 8 h without catecholamines
dosage.d: Taper by 0.005 units/min every hour as tolerated
dosage.n: Monitor for reversible diabetes insipidus after stopping

admin: Dilute 20 units/mL vial in normal saline (0.9%) or 5% dextrose to 0.1 units/mL (no fluid restriction) or 1 unit/mL (fluid restriction)
Inspect for particulate matter and discoloration before use
Discard unused diluted solution after 18 hours at room temperature or 24 hours refrigerated
Titrate to the lowest dose compatible with a clinically acceptable response
moa: Vasopressin causes vasoconstriction by binding to V1 receptors on vascular smooth muscle coupled to the Gq/phospholipase C-phosphatidyl-inositol-triphosphate pathway, resulting in release of intracellular calcium. In addition, vasopressin stimulates antidiuresis via stimulation of V2 receptors which are coupled to adenyl cyclase.

absolute: Known allergy or hypersensitivity to 8-L-arginine vasopressin (the 1 mL single-dose vial without chlorobutanol)
relative: Pre-existing impaired cardiac function (vasopressin can decrease cardiac index)
monitor: Cardiac index and hemodynamics during infusion
Serum electrolytes, fluid status, and urine output after discontinuation

preg: There are no available data on vasopressin injection use in pregnant women to inform a drug-associated risk; animal reproduction studies have not been conducted. Because placental vasopressinase increases clearance, the dose may need to be increased in the second and third trimesters. Vasopressin injection may produce tonic uterine contractions that could threaten the continuation of pregnancy.
lact: The labeling does not provide data on the presence of vasopressin in human milk, effects on the breastfed infant, or effects on milk production for this indication. A decision should weigh the clinical need against potential risk.
renal: Vasopressin is predominantly metabolized and only about 6% of the dose is excreted unchanged in urine; no specific renal dose adjustment is stated. Acute renal insufficiency has been reported as an adverse reaction.
hepatic: No specific hepatic dose adjustment is described in the labeling; increased bilirubin levels have been reported as an adverse reaction.

moderate: Catecholamines - additive pressor effect; monitor hemodynamics and adjust dose
Indomethacin - may prolong vasopressin's effect on cardiac index and systemic vascular resistance
Ganglionic blocking agents - may increase the pressor effect on mean arterial pressure
Drugs causing SIADH (SSRIs, TCAs, haloperidol, chlorpropamide, enalapril, methyldopa, pentamidine, vincristine, cyclophosphamide, ifosfamide, felbamate) - may increase pressor and antidiuretic effect
Drugs causing diabetes insipidus (demeclocycline, lithium, foscarnet, clozapine) - may decrease pressor and antidiuretic effect
interactions.diagnostics: Monitor serum sodium (hyponatremia risk) and hemodynamics

emergency: Ventricular tachyarrhythmias including Torsade de Pointes (overdose)
Severe ischemia / limb or organ infarction

monitoring: Mean arterial / blood pressure and hemodynamic response
Fluid status and urine output, particularly after discontinuation
Signs of ischemia (skin, digits, mesenteric, cardiac)
counsel: This medicine is given by continuous infusion in an intensive-care setting to support blood pressure
Your blood pressure, heart, and blood salts will be monitored closely
After it is stopped you may temporarily pass large amounts of dilute urine, which the team will manage
Report any chest pain, cold or discolored fingers/toes, or abdominal pain
pk: Pressor effect develops promptly during infusion
Steady-state plasma concentrations reached after about 30 minutes of continuous IV infusion
Apparent half-life 10 minutes or less at vasodilatory-shock infusion rates
Direct effects resolve within minutes of stopping the infusion
Store between 2 C and 8 C (36-46 F); do not freeze; once at room temperature use within 12 months
pearls: Second-line vasopressor for vasodilatory/septic shock unresponsive to fluids and catecholamines; effect is additive with catecholamines
Titrate to the lowest effective dose; ischemic complications increase at higher doses
May lower cardiac index - monitor cardiac function
Reversible diabetes insipidus (polyuria, dilute urine, hypernatremia) can occur after stopping; monitor sodium and urine output
Clearance increases markedly in late pregnancy due to placental vasopressinase, so the dose may need to be raised
missed: Not applicable - vasopressin injection is administered as a continuous, titrated infusion by clinicians in critical care, not on a fixed self-administered schedule.
overdose: Overdose manifests as consequences of vasoconstriction of various vascular beds (peripheral, mesenteric, coronary) and as hyponatremia. Less commonly it may cause ventricular tachyarrhythmias (including Torsade de Pointes), rhabdomyolysis, and nonspecific gastrointestinal symptoms. Direct effects resolve within minutes of withdrawal of treatment; provide supportive care and monitor hemodynamics and electrolytes.
